source.title: Safe crossover of neural networks through neuron alignment

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether same-architecture networks trained from different initializations share alignable representations, using neuron correlation and CCA alignment and measuring crossover outcomes. It does not test convergence with model scale.
record.gate_note: The paper reports neuron-relationship counts and outcomes of interpolating aligned or unaligned networks. The general claim that same-data networks learn similar representations is also attributed to earlier work; those cited results are not recorded as rows. Figure 3 plots averages over 200 pairs, but most curve values are not stated numerically in the text.
record.test_reason: This is mainly a crossover-method paper, close to T4. It still reports its own results on whether independently initialized same-architecture networks share neurons and features: 125 significant CCA relationships and 203 neuron pairs at r≥0.7 per MNIST pair. It also reports whether permutation-aligned networks can be interpolated with low loss. Both bear on V3 and on part of V4, in a new setting of small MLPs used for neuroevolution crossover.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that aligning neurons (SC-PwC, SC-CCA) before arithmetic crossover significantly outperforms naive crossover on MNIST and CIFAR-10 and preserves the parents' representations. They also say MNIST suggests a one-to-one neuron correspondence, which CIFAR-10 does not show. The paper also claims some offspring beat the parents' validation loss, and leaves CNNs and harder datasets to future work.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies neuron matching and parameter-space crossover between same-architecture networks trained from different initializations. It does not test the original scale- or cross-modal convergence claim.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes differ by dataset and matching method. The preferred SVCCA direction count differs between MNIST and CIFAR-10; changing λ across 0.01, 0.1, and 1 did not change the reported comparisons.

fits_no_version.finding: How well aligned networks can be interpolated depends on the alignment method and dataset. SVCCA with 256 directions helps on MNIST but not on CIFAR-10, pairwise correlation beats CCA on MNIST and loses on CIFAR-10, and the λ value of ridge CCA does not matter.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The success of permutation alignment for weight interpolation depends on the neuron-matching method and the dataset.

record.peer_reviewed: Annual Conference on Genetic and Evolutionary Computation (GECCO ’20)
record.problems: Evidence is limited to fully connected feed-forward networks of one architecture per dataset, trained on the same dataset from different initializations. Most crossover-path values are only plotted; exact textual values are limited. The authors describe the work as a proof of concept and leave state-of-the-art architectures and more complex datasets for future research.
record.rows_left_out: Figure 3 includes comparisons of SC-PwC bipartite matching and semi-matching in panels (e) and (f), but the text gives no outcome for those curves and their values are figure-only; they were not extracted as separate rows.

untested.parts: No variation in scale or capability, and no comparison across architectures, objectives or data.
Only small MLPs (1×512 on MNIST, 3×100 on CIFAR-10) trained on the same data; no convolutional or larger nets, and no random-network baseline.
Only permutation alignment followed by weight interpolation was tested. Linear maps between activations, stitching, relative representations and unpaired mapping were not.
No comparison of similarity measures on the same quantity, and no out-of-distribution inputs.
No test of shared data versus different data or objectives, and no plateau analysis.

record.verdict_notes: This is borderline T4: the paper's aim is a neuroevolution crossover operator. The V3 evidence rests on the counts in Section 5.2.2, which have no control (for example untrained or random networks). The V6 links and labels from the reader were removed because the method dependence concerns crossover outcome, not measured similarity. The reader's V6 label also cited r9, which was not linked to V6.

versions.untested_parts: No sweep over model size or capability, and no comparison across architectures, objectives, datasets, or modalities.
No vision-language or paired image-caption models.
Tests same-architecture feed-forward networks trained on the same dataset from different initializations; does not establish convergence across architectures, datasets, modalities, or scale.
Tests neuron permutation alignment followed by arithmetic interpolation of weights. Does not test linear activation maps, stitching, relative representations, or unpaired-data mapping.
No interpretable features, neurons, or circuits are identified or compared.
Compares correlation/CCA approaches and some settings on MNIST and CIFAR-10. Does not test out-of-distribution inputs or a broad range of input datasets.
Does not compare shared versus different training data or objectives, nor quantify an alignment plateau.
